questions.prompt: The model read config.ts, then you saved the file in your editor, then the model sends an edit. What happens?
options: The edit is applied to your new version
The edit is refused because the file's version changed since it was read, and the model is told to re-read
The model's old copy overwrites your change
The edit waits until you close the editor
questions.explanation: The size or modification time no longer matches the stored version, so the edit is refused as stale instead of working from an outdated view.

questions.prompt: old_string appears twice and replace_all is false. Why refuse instead of replacing the first one?
options: Because replacing text twice is slower
Because the tool cannot count matches reliably
Because guessing which occurrence was meant is how the wrong line gets changed
Because the schema forbids repeated text
questions.explanation: With two matches the tool cannot know which one the model meant, so it asks for a more specific old_string or an explicit replace_all.

questions.prompt: Why write to a temporary file and then rename it over the original?
options: A rename happens completely or not at all, so a crash never leaves a half-written file
Because writeFile cannot overwrite existing files
So the old version is kept as a backup
Because renaming is the only way to change a file's modification time
questions.explanation: If the program dies while writing the temp file, the original is untouched. The rename then swaps in the finished file in one step.
